items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Art Hodes, Dick Carey, Ellis Larkins and Sammy Price, pianists.

ctx.x: When we received the next pay check, there was a message in it, telling us that we had two more weeks in the Club. Barney thought that we deserved a raise, and he raised us out of the joint. Later, we learned that Gene Fields had replaced us, but we didn't hold any animosity towards Gene, because it was the same like it was played in the music field, and we still had a ball while we were at the Cafe Society Uptown.

On June 15th, there was one of the biggest concerts ever given anywhere at that time. It was in Philadelphia, and was sponsored by Sammy Price, the boogie and blues pianist, and Dan Burley, a reporter for a Negro newspaper in New York, "The Amsterdam News", who was also a pianist and exponent of a rhythm called scuffle. They formed the Basin Street Swing Club and for this session which started at 1.30 pm and finished at 6 pm, part of the line-up was Sidney de Paris, Chelsea Qualey, Jack Butler, and myself,…

It was in December 1943 that I made records with the great Lester Young. I had first met him when I was on tour with the Ralph Cooper orchestra in 1932 in Denver, Colorado. We were playing a theatre, and after finishing that, there was a dance. After the dance, the musicians came to the place where we were living which was known as a popular musicians hangout. The band that had played for the dance was the Blue Devils, with whom Lester Young was playing saxophone. We started a jam session, and that was when I…
